points.quote: and document how the force threshold relates to the real procedure.
points.fix: Documented in README Fidelity and task.json fidelity. Source: the maker's own procedure (Mitutoyo Gauge Blocks Quick Guide, linked in the README) says to rotate the blocks 'while applying slight force' and publishes no figure; we found no published figure in newtons. The 3 N floor is therefore a chosen one and stated as such: about five times the 25 mm block's own weight (0.6 N), so resting or brushing the block never counts, and under the roughly 6 N at which this rig's pinched block pivots in the pads. A real trial reads the same threshold on the filmed scale: at least 306 g (3 N) above tare through the turn. The round-2 decision named only the tilt limit as still open.

points.quote: Please require face-to-face contact throughout the pressed turn
points.fix: Required at ALL corners and at EVERY step: every corner of the overlap patch within 0.05 mm of the 50 mm block's face at each control step of the counted turn; one step outside restarts the turn. Why 0.05 mm and not zero: (1) rigid bodies have no oil film or surface give, so a block pressed and turned by a compliant arm never sits at exactly zero: in the demo's pressed, levelled turn the corners read 0.003 mm typically and up to 0.045 mm for single steps, and a 0.02 mm limit breaks such a turn (Isaac runs 4-6 failed at 0.02 mm; run 5 broke 14 times on readings of 0.020-0.037 mm with the tilt under 0.25 deg and no lift); (2) the simulator's own contact test is far looser: it creates contact points from 1 mm away (contact_offset), so 'the solver reports contact at every corner' would have accepted the reviewer's 0.24 mm case; (3) the real-trial equivalent: 0.05 mm is the thinnest leaf of a common feeler set, 0.32 deg across the 9 mm face, about five times tighter than the reviewer's 0.24 mm case. After the turn the contact must also last: leaving the face (any of the block's four lower corners more than 1 mm off its plane, slid off it, or more than 20 mm off centre) loses the wringing for good.

known_limits: Face to face is a band, not zero: a step counts with every corner of the overlap within 0.05 mm of the face (0.32 deg across the 9 mm face; about five times tighter than the 0.24 mm one-edge gap named in the review). A block riding one edge with the other up to 0.05 mm clear therefore still counts. In this run the largest gap at a step that added turn was 0.038 mm (0.003 mm median at the trace samples after the block settled).

The 5 mm hands-off fence checks each arm link's corners against the plate and platform, and points about 20 mm apart on them against each link. A flat link laid across the plate's top rim midway between two points (a pocket about 1.4 mm long and 3 deg wide) reads hands-off while resting on the plate, so a press made there could load the scale. Found by our own check after this run; rim points every 2 mm close it in later code that has no simulator run on the GPU yet, so it is not in this package.
After the turn the wringing survives a lift of under 1 mm at every corner; a real trial settles it with the hand lift test.
